name: Explaining what a model's prediction came from
gist: When a model makes a decision, which inputs mattered most? These papers trace back through the computation to credit the right parts of the input for the output.
explain: When a model makes a prediction, we want to know why. If a language model generates the word 'happy' as the next token, which parts of the input influenced that choice? Was it a specific adjective two sentences back? A pattern in the overall sentiment? These papers compute importance scores: a number for each input element (word, pixel, etc.) telling how much that element contributed to the final answer. This is called attribution or explainability — the goal is to justify the prediction in terms of the input.

Attribution is tricky because causality in neural networks is tangled. Removing one input word changes many neurons, which affect many other computations downstream. Does the importance score measure the direct effect or the total effect? Different methods give different answers. Some use gradient-based methods: how much does the output change if we nudge the input slightly? Others use perturbation: mask inputs and see what breaks. The papers in this area refine these techniques and study when they work and when they fail. The use case is critical: in medicine or law, you need to explain decisions, and a model that points to the relevant evidence is more trustworthy than one that stays silent.

papers.title: A model of errors in transformers
papers.contribution: The model provides excellent agreement between predicted and observed accuracy across Gemini, DeepSeek, and other models on repetitive tasks, with alternative explanations to reasoning collapse.

papers.title: An In-Depth Study on Deep Learning Model Cloning
papers.contribution: First definition of model cloning with a method for model similarity detection; demonstrates accurate detection on synthetic model clone benchmark and real-world open-source models.

papers.title: Dyslexify: A Mechanistic Defense Against Typographic Attacks in CLIP
papers.contribution: Improves performance up to 22.06% on a typographic ImageNet-100 variant while reducing standard accuracy by <1%, serving as a training-free defense for safety-critical applications.

papers.title: Evaluating Data Influence in Meta Learning
papers.contribution: Our framework provides closed-form solutions for task and instance influence functions, with strategies to enhance computational efficiency and scalability.

papers.title: Hallucination Begins Where Saliency Drops
papers.contribution: Significantly reduces hallucinations via inference-time filtering and module-based attention strengthening, offering interpretable hallucination detection.

papers.title: Manifold-Aligned Guided Integrated Gradients for Reliable Feature Attribution
papers.contribution: Produces faithful explanations by aggregating gradients on path features proximal to input, reducing off-manifold noise and outperforming prior path-based attribution methods.

papers.title: Shapley Regularized Neural Granger Causality
papers.contribution: Demonstrates robust causal relationship recovery on synthetic and realistic datasets with flexible model-agnostic regularizers that can integrate into any differentiable neural network.

papers.title: TN-SHAP-G: Graph-Structured Tensor Network Surrogates for Shapley Values and Interactions
papers.contribution: Matches exact Shapley values on small graphs and scales to large graphs where sampling methods fail, demonstrating efficient factorization.

papers.title: $\texttt{ShaplEIG}$: Bayesian Experimental Design for Shapley Value Estimation
papers.contribution: Provides closed-form expected information gain via linearity of Shapley values; reduces complexity from exponential to polynomial in player count via elementary symmetric polynomials; consistently improves sample efficiency.

papers.title: Addressing divergent representations from causal interventions on neural networks
papers.contribution: The method reduces pernicious divergences that activate hidden pathways while maintaining the explanatory value of interventions for interpretability.

papers.title: An Odd Estimator for Shapley Values
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art Shapley value estimation accuracy at larger sampling budgets compared to paired sampling approaches.

papers.title: Bayesian Influence Functions for Hessian-Free Data Attribution
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results on predicting retraining experiments while scaling efficiently to billion-parameter neural networks.

papers.title: DecodeShare: Tracing the Shared Subspace of LLM Decode-Time Decisions
papers.contribution: Demonstrates the discovered decode-shared subspace is a high-leverage causal channel; removing it degrades performance far more than removing a random subspace, enabling more reliable activation steering for downstream deployment.

papers.title: Discovering Interpretable Algorithms by Decompiling Transformers to RASP
papers.contribution: Recovers simple and interpretable RASP programs from length-generalizing transformers on algorithmic and formal language tasks.

papers.title: Dissecting Representation Misalignment in Contrastive Learning via Influence Function
papers.contribution: Advances transparency of CLIP-style models by offering more accurate assessment of data impact and model alignment for data evaluation, misalignment detection, and misprediction trace-back compared to traditional influence functions.

papers.title: ExPLAIND: Unifying Model, Data, and Training Attribution to Study Model Behavior
papers.contribution: Reveals learning phases in Grokking and two-phase dynamics in EuroLLM pretraining, establishing a unified framework for interpreting model behavior and training dynamics.

papers.title: Exactly Computing do-Shapley Values
papers.contribution: Achieves exact computation of do-Shapley values with orders of magnitude improvement in accuracy compared to prior estimators, while reducing identification burden to only singleton coalition interventions.

papers.title: First is Not Really Better Than Last: Evaluating Layer Choice and Aggregation Strategies in Language Model Data Influence Estimation
papers.contribution: Demonstrates that middle attention layers provide superior data influence estimation compared to first layers, with improved aggregation methods and evaluation metrics.

papers.title: Functional Decomposition and Shapley Interactions for Interpreting Survival Models
papers.contribution: Provides principled interaction-aware and time-aware interpretability for survival modeling with applications in cancer prognosis.

papers.title: GUDA: Counterfactual Group-wise Training Data Attribution for Diffusion Models via Unlearning
papers.contribution: Identifies primary contributing groups more reliably than semantic similarity and gradient approaches with ~100× speedup over LOGO retraining.

papers.title: Influence Dynamics and Stagewise Data Attribution
papers.contribution: The study confirms that token-level influence changes in language models align with known developmental stages, with influence driven by the model's progressive learning of semantic hierarchies.

papers.title: Joint Distribution–Informed Shapley Values for Sparse Counterfactual Explanations
papers.contribution: COLA achieves the same target effects with only 26-45% of the original feature edits across four datasets, twelve models, and five CE generators.

papers.title: Learning to Weight Parameters for Training Data Attribution
papers.contribution: The method improves attribution accuracy across image classification, language modeling, and diffusion tasks while enabling fine-grained attribution for concepts like subject and style.

papers.title: Linear Mechanisms for Spatiotemporal Reasoning in Vision Language Models
papers.contribution: Reveals linear spatiotemporal ID mechanism in VLMs, extends analysis to video VLMs identifying temporal IDs, providing diagnostic tool for model limitations.

papers.title: Mechanistic Data Attribution: Tracing the Training Origins of Interpretable LLM Units
papers.contribution: MDA causally demonstrates that repetitive structural data acts as a mechanistic catalyst and provides direct evidence linking induction heads to in-context learning (ICL) capability.

papers.title: Missingness Bias Calibration in Feature Attribution Explanations
papers.contribution: MCal consistently reduces missingness bias across diverse medical benchmarks spanning vision, language, and tabular domains, competitive with or outperforming heavyweight approaches.

papers.title: Nonparametric Data Attribution for Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms existing nonparametric baselines and achieves best attribution performance among methods that do not use target-model parameters or gradients while producing spatially interpretable attributions.

papers.title: PINNfluence: Interpreting PINNs through Influence Functions
papers.contribution: Demonstrates influence patterns provide granular diagnostics distinguishing structural characteristics across well-trained and poorly-trained PINNs, opening new interpretability avenue.

papers.title: PolySHAP: Extending KernelSHAP with Interaction-Informed Polynomial Regression
papers.contribution: PolySHAP yields empirically better Shapley value estimates and proves that paired sampling outputs identical estimates to second-order PolySHAP.

papers.title: Priority-Aware Shapley Value
papers.contribution: Recovers precedence-only and weight-only variants as special cases; demonstrates more structure-faithful allocations on data valuation and feature attribution with practical sensitivity analysis via priority sweeping.

papers.title: Singular Vectors of Attention Heads Align with Features
papers.contribution: Establishes alignment of singular vectors with features as a sound and theoretically justified basis for feature identification in language models.

papers.title: Step-Resolved Data Attribution for Looped Transformers
papers.contribution: Scales excellently at transformer scale with per-step insights into latent reasoning process.

papers.title: Testing Most Influential Sets
papers.contribution: Rigorous hypothesis tests for excessive influence replace ad-hoc heuristics across economics, biology, and ML benchmarks.

papers.title: Tracing and Reversing Edits in LLMs
papers.contribution: Successfully reverses up to 94% of edits and restores original model output distribution without edit information.

papers.title: TreeGrad-Ranker: Feature Ranking via $O(L)$-Time Gradients for Decision Trees
papers.contribution: TreeGrad-Ranker produces feature rankings satisfying key axioms while achieving numerical error 10^15 times lower than Linear TreeShap for Shapley values.

papers.title: Understanding the Emergence of Seemingly Useless Features in Next-Token Predictors
papers.contribution: Features with extremely high or low influence on future tokens relate to formal reasoning domains like code; this work steps toward understanding hidden features through lens of development during training.

papers.title: Verified SHAP: Provable Bounds for Exact Shapley Values of Neural Networks
papers.contribution: Scales exact SHAP computation to orders of magnitude larger feature spaces than state-of-the-art exact methods, establishing principled foundation for evaluating approximation methods.

papers.title: What LLMs Explain Is Not What They Believe: Evaluating Explanation Sufficiency Under Models' Own Input Beliefs
papers.contribution: Introduce self-consistent sufficiency metric (SCSuff) showing LLM explanations are generally insufficient and weakly correlated with model size.
